title: Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend and the labour market
extraction: docs/design/research/alaska-pfd-case.md (every number has a page reference there; NOT VERIFIED items are listed in that file)

citation.title: The Labor Market Impacts of Universal and Permanent Cash Transfers: Evidence from the Alaska Permanent Fund
citation.published: American Economic Journal: Economic Policy 14(2): 315-340, May 2022
citation.editionUsed: AEJ 2022 typeset article + online appendix (May 2021); NBER w24312 rev. Jan 2020 for the superseded calibration
citation.replication: Bacher et al. (2022), Institute for Replication, Oslo Replication Games

treatment.unit: State of Alaska (one treated unit; donors: 49 other states + DC)
treatment.definition: Introduction of the universal annual dividend (first paid 1982). On/off regime, not dose-response.

method.estimator: Synthetic control (Abadie, Diamond & Hainmueller 2010), outcome-specific weights; estimand = mean post-period gap
method.inference: Permutation over 51 states x placebo years 1978-2013 (1,836 placebos; 1,734 for hours), two-tailed; 95% CI by test inversion
method.caution: The authors note randomisation is unlikely to describe the data-generating process (AEJ p.322). I4R shows estimates vary with post-period length and estimator.

fundingBoundary: Permanent Fund investment earnings (oil-royalty origin); 'not explicitly financed by taxes' (AEJ p.336). No tax-side effects are in the estimate. State income tax repealed 1980; 1980 placebo null (AEJ-OA Table A.8).

outcomes.label: Part-time rate
outcomes.fragility: p 0.059 with state-only placebos; +0.011 (p 0.101) with common weights; +0.009 (p 0.141) controlling for oil; I4R +0.003 to +0.011 with covariates

mappings.classification: reproduction of the authors' own calibration, compared with their estimate
mappings.independence: Not independent: the same authors published the calibration beside the estimate and revised its inputs between editions (MPC 0.25 -> 0.5, kappa 1.2 -> 0.9, per-person -> per-household PDV). No parameter here was chosen by this repository.
mappings.applicability: Small (7% of labour income), resource-funded, one state, not countercyclical.

mappings.classification: structural check of the simulator's world model
mappings.note: The world engine has no labour-supply or local-demand response to transfers; the check verifies that by running it, rather than asserting it. A zero here is a missing mechanism, not a prediction of zero.

mappings.reason: Neither the calibration nor the world engine has an intensive margin or a part-time state.
No participation margin in either model; the world engine's unemployment is displacement-driven only.
No hours variable in either model.
No sectors. The authors' own evidence here is weak (pre-fit worse than 99% of placebos).
No sectors. Pre-fit worse than 99% of placebos.

limits: Small transfer: the authors say the effect of UBI-sized payments (e.g. USD 1,000/month) is uncertain (AEJ p.337).
Resource-rent funded: no tax-side distortions are in the estimate.
The general-equilibrium channel is not directly tested (AEJ p.316).
Average over 33 years with a 5-year pre-period; the part-time effect is near zero in 1982-85 and grows.
Not a micro elasticity: within-Alaska designs find negative hours effects (Feinberg & Kuehn 2018); different estimand.
